newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Some length absorbed by bunkers.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Some length absorbed by bunkers.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices edged up with some supplies finding outlets into China and the bunker markets, traders said on Friday.
A bunker trader bought a major's 180-cst cargo at $98.00 per tonne fob lifting February 11-15.
Traders said bunker demand, particularly on Thursday, was very healthy and at least three majors were said to be sold out of January supplies.

Also two to three 20,000-tonne cargoes were said sold into China this week at around $7.00 per tonne over Singapore quotes on a cost-and-freight basis to South China, for delivery second-half february.
"But this is the last of the Chinese demand prior to the New Year," complained one major.
Singapore fob cargoes were assessed at minus 75 cents to plus 75 cents for 180-cst and 380-cst material for the bunker market was assessed at minus $2.00-$2.50, traders said.
Another major in Singapore offered a cargo at $102 for later timings of February 16-20.
